rounds.title: Seed Of The Woman
rounds.prophecySummary: The serpent's head would be bruised by the woman's seed.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: It shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Christ is presented as defeating the devil through death.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: That through death he might destroy him that had the power of death.
rounds.teachingNote: This is commonly read by Christian interpreters as an early promise of victory over evil.

rounds.title: Blessing To All Nations
rounds.prophecySummary: All families of the earth would be blessed through Abram.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Paul connects the promise to the gospel blessing reaching Gentiles.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: In thee shall all nations be blessed.
rounds.teachingNote: The New Testament explicitly applies this Abraham promise to the gospel going to the nations.

rounds.title: Ruler From Judah
rounds.prophecySummary: The sceptre is associated with Judah and a coming ruler.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Jesus is identified as coming from the tribe of Judah.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: Our Lord sprang out of Juda.
rounds.teachingNote: The Judah connection is a widely recognized messianic theme.

rounds.title: Prophet Like Moses
rounds.prophecySummary: The Lord would raise up a prophet like Moses.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Peter quotes this prophecy while preaching about Christ.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you.
rounds.teachingNote: Acts gives this passage a direct place in apostolic preaching about Jesus.

rounds.title: Son And King
rounds.prophecySummary: The anointed king is addressed as God's Son.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Paul quotes Psalm 2 in connection with Jesus being raised up.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.
rounds.teachingNote: Psalm 2 is used in the New Testament to speak of the Messiah's sonship and reign.

rounds.title: Not Seeing Corruption
rounds.prophecySummary: The Holy One would not be left to corruption.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: Neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Peter says this was spoken of Christ's resurrection.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: His soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption.
rounds.teachingNote: Acts 2 directly connects Psalm 16 with the resurrection of Jesus.

rounds.title: Suffering Cry
rounds.prophecySummary: The psalm opens with a cry of being forsaken.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Jesus speaks this line from the cross.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
rounds.teachingNote: The Gospel records Jesus using Psalm 22 language during the crucifixion.

rounds.title: Garments Divided
rounds.prophecySummary: Garments are parted and lots are cast.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Soldiers cast lots for Jesus' garment.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: They said therefore among themselves, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it.
rounds.teachingNote: John explicitly cites the casting of lots as fulfillment of scripture.

rounds.title: Bones Not Broken
rounds.prophecySummary: The righteous sufferer's bones are preserved.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Jesus' bones were not broken at the crucifixion.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: A bone of him shall not be broken.
rounds.teachingNote: John cites this detail while describing Jesus' death.

rounds.title: Betrayed By A Friend
rounds.prophecySummary: A familiar friend lifts up his heel against the speaker.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: Mine own familiar friend... hath lifted up his heel against me.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Jesus applies the text to betrayal within his circle.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me.
rounds.teachingNote: John records Jesus citing the psalm in the context of Judas's betrayal.

rounds.title: Zeal For God's House
rounds.prophecySummary: Zeal for the Lord's house consumes the speaker.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: The disciples remember this scripture after Jesus cleanses the temple.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.
rounds.teachingNote: John presents the temple cleansing through the lens of Psalm 69.

rounds.title: Vinegar Given
rounds.prophecySummary: The suffering figure receives gall and vinegar.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: In my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Jesus is given vinegar during the crucifixion.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: They filled a spunge with vinegar... and put it to his mouth.
rounds.teachingNote: The Gospels connect this detail with Jesus' crucifixion.

rounds.title: At God's Right Hand
rounds.prophecySummary: The Lord invites David's Lord to sit at His right hand.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: Sit thou at my right hand.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: The verse is applied to the exalted Son.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
rounds.teachingNote: Psalm 110 is one of the New Testament's most frequent messianic texts.

rounds.title: Rejected Stone
rounds.prophecySummary: The rejected stone becomes the head of the corner.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Peter applies the rejected stone to Jesus.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: The stone which was set at nought of you builders.
rounds.teachingNote: Acts directly applies the stone image to Jesus' rejection and exaltation.

rounds.title: Virgin-Born Sign
rounds.prophecySummary: A child called Immanuel is given as a sign.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Matthew quotes the sign in connection with Jesus' birth.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: They shall call his name Emmanuel.
rounds.teachingNote: Matthew explicitly quotes Isaiah 7:14 in the infancy narrative.

rounds.title: Light In Galilee
rounds.prophecySummary: Light comes to Galilee and people in darkness.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Matthew connects Jesus' Galilean ministry with Isaiah's words.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: The people which sat in darkness saw great light.
rounds.teachingNote: The Gospel citation ties the prophecy to Jesus' public ministry in Galilee.

rounds.title: Child And Kingdom
rounds.prophecySummary: A child is born whose government and peace increase.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: Unto us a child is born... and the government shall be upon his shoulder.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Gabriel announces Davidic rule and an everlasting kingdom.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: He shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever.
rounds.teachingNote: Luke's announcement uses Davidic kingdom language that Christians connect with Isaiah's promise.

rounds.title: Voice In The Wilderness
rounds.prophecySummary: A voice prepares the way of the Lord in the wilderness.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: Prepare ye the way of the Lord.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: John the Baptist is identified with the wilderness voice.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: The voice of one crying in the wilderness.
rounds.teachingNote: The Synoptic Gospels connect Isaiah 40:3 with John the Baptist.

rounds.title: Chosen Servant
rounds.prophecySummary: The servant is upheld by God and brings judgment to the Gentiles.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Matthew quotes the servant passage in relation to Jesus' ministry.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: Behold my servant, whom I have chosen.
rounds.teachingNote: Matthew's quotation presents Jesus' ministry through Isaiah's servant language.

rounds.title: Despised And Rejected
rounds.prophecySummary: The servant is despised, rejected, and acquainted with grief.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: He is despised and rejected of men.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: John says Jesus came to his own, and his own received him not.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: He came unto his own, and his own received him not.
rounds.teachingNote: This pairing is thematic rather than a direct quotation, so the wording stays careful.

rounds.title: Wounded For Transgressions
rounds.prophecySummary: The servant is wounded and bruised for others.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: He was wounded for our transgressions.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Peter applies the servant's suffering to Christ's death.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: By whose stripes ye were healed.
rounds.teachingNote: 1 Peter explicitly uses Isaiah 53 language for Christ's suffering.

rounds.title: Silent Before Accusers
rounds.prophecySummary: The servant is oppressed yet does not open his mouth.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: He opened not his mouth.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Jesus gives no answer before Pilate's accusations.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: He answered him to never a word.
rounds.teachingNote: The Gospel scene is a widely recognized fulfillment connection to Isaiah 53.

rounds.title: With The Rich In Death
rounds.prophecySummary: The servant is associated with the rich in his death.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: With the rich in his death.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Joseph of Arimathaea, a rich man, buries Jesus in his tomb.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: A rich man of Arimathaea... laid it in his own new tomb.
rounds.teachingNote: Matthew's burial account is commonly read with Isaiah 53:9.

rounds.title: Numbered With Transgressors
rounds.prophecySummary: The servant is numbered with transgressors.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: He was numbered with the transgressors.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Jesus quotes this line before his arrest.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: He was reckoned among the transgressors.
rounds.teachingNote: Luke records Jesus explicitly quoting this line about what must be accomplished.

rounds.title: Bethlehem Ruler
rounds.prophecySummary: A ruler for Israel comes from Bethlehem.
rounds.prophecyTextShort: Out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel.
rounds.fulfillmentSummary: Chief priests and scribes identify Bethlehem when Herod asks about Messiah's birth.
rounds.fulfillmentTextShort: In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet.
rounds.teachingNote: Matthew directly links Messiah's birthplace with Micah 5:2.
